reason: The passage emphasizes hierarchy through multiple narrative and linguistic elements. David is portrayed as a military commander with authority over 400 men, issuing orders that are obeyed without question. More significantly, the text repeatedly emphasizes the hierarchical relationship through Abigail's deference: she prostrates herself before David multiple times ('וַתִּפֹּל לְאַפֵּי דָוִד עַל־ פָּנֶיהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּחוּ אָרֶץ' - 'fell on her face before David and bowed to the ground'), addresses him as 'my lord' (אֲדֹנִי), and repeatedly identifies herself as his servant/handmaid (אֲמָתְךָ). The text further encourages proper hierarchy by presenting Abigail's acknowledgment of David's authority as the wise, virtuous course of action that prevents violence and is rewarded by David's respect and later marriage. The narrative validates hierarchical relationships as appropriate and right.
